claim: Flow Matching regresses the network vector field onto the vector field that generates a target probability path
The posterior-weighted average of conditional vector fields generates the marginal probability path
value: Theorem 1 (marginal VF of Eq. 8 generates marginal path of Eq. 6)

claim: Conditional Flow Matching uses per-sample paths and vector fields, so unbiased estimates are cheap
CFM and FM losses are equal up to a theta-independent constant, so their gradients are identical
Conditional probability paths are Gaussians with time-dependent mean and scalar std, from N(0,I) at t=0 to N(x_1, sigma_min^2 I) at t=1
value: p_t(x|x_1) = N(x | mu_t(x_1), sigma_t(x_1)^2 I); mu_0=0, sigma_0=1, mu_1=x_1, sigma_1=sigma_min

claim: The unique vector field of the affine Gaussian flow psi_t(x) = sigma_t x + mu_t has closed form
VE and VP diffusion paths are special cases; the resulting VP conditional field coincides with the probability flow ODE field
value: VP: mu_t = alpha_{1-t} x_1, sigma_t = sqrt(1 - alpha_{1-t}^2)
loc: Sec 4.1 Example I, Eq. (16)-(19); Appendix D

claim: The optimal transport conditional path moves mean and std linearly in time, giving straight constant-speed trajectories
value: mu_t = t x_1, sigma_t = 1 - (1 - sigma_min) t; u_t(x|x_1) = (x_1 - (1 - sigma_min) x) / (1 - (1 - sigma_min) t)

claim: With the OT path the CFM regression target is constant in time
value: target x_1 - (1 - sigma_min) x_0 at point psi_t(x_0) = (1 - (1 - sigma_min) t) x_0 + t x_1

claim: Numeric value of sigma_min used in experiments
value: not stated in v2 (only 'set sufficiently small')

claim: ImageNet 32x32: OT path beats diffusion path under Flow Matching and all diffusion baselines
value: FM-OT NLL 3.53, FID 5.02, NFE 122; FM-Diffusion 3.54, 6.37, 193; Score Matching 3.56, 5.68, 178
